operator: index.html: the step counter is position:absolute and picks up the description span's padding-left, so 1, 2, 3 are painted over the first letter of each command name (three pairs); the must-pass twin gives the counter its own grid column and names the description span. Both twins carry adjacent two-column text (touching, not overlapping), a <b> inside a paragraph (containment), and an ins.adsbygoogle block whose two children overlap on purpose: the third-party exclusion must keep the probe silent on it. The must-pass twin also carries the two shapes that made the probe report six false pairs on uxcli's own dashboard (v1.3): two run names ellipsised by `overflow:hidden` whose unclipped text would reach the timestamp beside them, and a list scrolling inside its own box whose first rows are cut away entirely. Both were reported as overlaps before text rects were clamped to their clipping ancestors; neither is painted where the probe said it was. It also carries a CLOSED <details> holding a run of JSON, with a line of text below it where that JSON would have been laid out: Chrome hides a closed disclosure with content-visibility, which no computed property the probe reads will report, and its descendants still answer getClientRects() — so the hidden packet was collected as painted text and "overlapped" the footer two hundred pixels below it, on uxcli's own run-detail screen.
